A free Note3 alternative: Rupok vs Note3

Note3 is Prestigio’s paid, Windows-only whiteboard software, the updated EasiNote. Rupok is free and open source, runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on any computer or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux, and adds AI-made lessons and class replay. Here’s an honest comparison.

Where Note3 is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

  • Ready-made STEM tools. Geometry and 3D shapes, electric circuits, chemistry apparatus and the periodic table are built in2,4. Rupok’s Smart Ink draws clean graphs and logic gates (and, once switched on in Settings, circuit symbols and benzene rings), and its presets gallery has ready-made physics and chemistry objects, but it has no ruler, protractor, compass, lab apparatus or periodic table yet. For those you ask your AI for a Smart Object.
  • Handwriting recognition without an AI account4. Rupok reads handwritten maths offline, but turning other handwriting into text needs your own Claude API key, and it can’t read Bangla handwriting yet.
  • Opens PowerPoint files directly and lets you annotate them4. In Rupok you save slides as PDF first.
  • More export formats: PPTX, DOCX and JPG as well as PDF4. Rupok exports PDF (slides or handouts).
  • Document-camera support4.

Where Rupok is stronger

  • Free on every device. No licence keys and no activation, so you can put it on every panel and laptop in your school.
  • Not just Windows. It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS, and as a free desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.
  • AI Smart Objects. Ask Claude or ChatGPT for a simulation or a quiz and it lands on your slide, live, ready to write on.
  • AI help on the board. Chat with your own Claude, Codex or OpenCode inside Rupok, or select a problem and tap Solve this: the AI writes a step-by-step solution in handwriting, and you check it before the class sees it.
  • Class replay. Every stroke is saved with its timing. Send the .rpk file to the class WhatsApp group; students replay it in their browser.
  • Bangla. Bangla text and fonts work in lessons, voice typing works in Bangla, and a Bangla interface is coming. Rupok is made in Bangladesh.
  • Open source, open format. Your lessons are never locked in.

Which one should you pick?

Pick Note3 if you teach on Windows, rely on its built-in geometry, physics and chemistry tools or on opening PowerPoint files directly, and are happy to buy a licence for each device.

Pick Rupok if you want one free tool on every board and laptop, interactive lessons made by AI, and replays your students can open on their phones.

You can also use both: export a Note3 lesson to PDF and teach it in Rupok.

Switching from Note3

  1. Export from Note3.Note3 exports lessons as PDF4.
  2. Open the board.Go to rupok.app/board in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? Download it for Windows, Mac or Linux.
  3. Drop the PDF in.Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
  4. Add the live parts.Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object (how).
  5. Save and share.Save the lesson as a .rpk file and send it to students. They replay it at rupok.app/open.
FAQ

Rupok and Note3: questions

Is there a free alternative to Note3?

Yes. Rupok is free and open source. It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on any computer connected to your smartboard or panel, with no licence key, activation or account.

Is Note3 the same as EasiNote?

Prestigio describes Note3 as the updated version of EasiNote, launched in July 20241. Its files use EasiNote’s .enb format4.

Can Rupok open Note3 (.enb) files?

No. Export the lesson from Note3 as a PDF and drop the PDF into Rupok; every page becomes a slide you can write on.

Does Rupok work on a Prestigio MultiBoard?

Rupok needs Chrome, Edge or Safari with WebGPU or WebGL2. On a panel with a Windows PC module or a connected computer, open rupok.app/board there, or install the Rupok desktop app (Windows, Mac or Linux). Whether a panel’s built-in Android browser is fast enough varies by model, so a PC is the safe choice.

Is Rupok legal to use for free in schools?

Yes. Rupok is open-source software under the AGPL-3.0. Any school can use it on any number of devices at no cost.
